title: Computing and Plotting a Binary Confusion Matrix
description: Compute the 2x2 confusion matrix cm from yc_test and y_pred with labels=[0,1] and render it with ConfusionMatrixDisplay.

steps.description: Compute the `2 x 2` matrix `cm = confusion_matrix(yc_test, y_pred, labels=[0,1])` and wrap it in `ConfusionMatrixDisplay` with `display_labels=['malignant','benign']`.
Call `disp.plot()`, set the plot title to `'Confusion Matrix'`, and display the figure with `plt.show()`.
Look at `labels=[0,1]` and `display_labels=['malignant','benign']`: row and column `0` correspond to `'malignant'`, and row and column `1` correspond to `'benign'`.

steps.question: With `labels=[0,1]` and positive class `benign` (`y = 1`), which entries of `cm` sit on the main diagonal (`cm[0, 0]` and `cm[1, 1]`), and which sit off the diagonal?
steps.answer: The main diagonal holds the correct predictions (`TN` at `cm[0, 0]` and `TP` at `cm[1, 1]`), while the off-diagonal entries hold the errors (`FP` at `cm[0, 1]` and `FN` at `cm[1, 0]`).
